notes.title: V.4, something something update
notes.content:
[h1]Hey there horror enthusiasts, this is the version 4 notes. We improved some things[/h1]

[h2]What's new:[/h2]

- We tried playing Freja with controllers. Turns out it works with controllers, but not perfectly. Navigating menus is a slight inconvenience, for example. But it works fine for the most part. Read more about which controllers it support on the store page

[h2]Patch notes:[/h2]

- Minor fixes to certain objects, like adding proper collision to an object you could previously walk through and fixing some visual glitches
- The flashlight is on when you pick it up in the first night scene now. It felt immersion breaking to pick up a flashlight that's clearly on, and then see it's off when you use it
- Fixed an issue with a door having poor soundmixing (being way louder than other sounds if you lowered the in-game volume)
- Fixed an object not moving with the rest of the room at the end of the Altered state chapter

notes.title: Movement Update
notes.content:
Several players mentioned sluggish mouse movement in the school scenes.
It has now been increased a lot and feels much smoother.

You should hopefully not have to adjust it at all, but I did add a sensitivity slider in the pause menu of each school scene just in case. However, there was an issue getting it to properly save, so if you want to lower the sensitivity, then you have to do so in each new scene. This will hopefully not be an issue in the future. I wanted to push this out now as I'd rather have a tiny inconvenience than the game being near unplayable for some.

Your feedback is much appreciated and more improvements will hopefully come in the future. Thank you, and stay spooked. ːdefiledskullː

notes.title: May update
notes.content:
Hey horror enthusiasts! We are now one week away from participating in a local game festival where we will showcase Freja to visitors and let people playtest it. As such, a big priority lately has been polishing what we already have to make an interesting playslice. The updated playslice might also be used for curators later on depending on how it goes at the festival. One part of the polishing has been improving the minigame "Mazerunner" to better integrate it into the story and make it look more unique with our own character and overall better environment design. In other words, it looks less like a bunch of placeholders and more like an actual minigame. 

[h1]What has been done since last update[/h1]

- Improved Mazerunner
- Polished a lot of the levels in the game
- Worked on the final levels of the game
- Implemented steam achievements

[h1]What to do moving forward[/h1]

We are hopefully looking at a summer release for the game. At least, that's what we're hoping for. The upcoming week will be spent polishing Freja further and then show it off at the festival. The feedback we get from it will hopefully be valuable and help us improve the game further. We will continue to work on the final parts of the game after that and begin testing everything and improve the performance. 

Happy early Mother's Day, and stay tuned! ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: April update
notes.content:
Hey horror enthusiasts! Hope you had a good easter.
Here are the latest news about Freja.

[h1]What has been done since last update[/h1]

- Worked further with the story and one of the minigames
- Designed the final area before the epilogue sequence will begin
- Fixed a sound related issue with one of the enemies
- Fixed the reported mouse cursor not getting locked on the game window issue
- Created more events around the levels
- New soundtracks and more soundeffects added

One thing we noticed in some of the gameplay videos was the effectiveness of soundeffects playing in the levels, so that is something we are definitely keeping!

[h1]What to do moving forward[/h1]

Apart from finishing the last bits of the game, we also need to see what we can do to improve performance in each level. We know of a few ways to do this already, but we are doing that last since each level is still getting updated every now and then, so doing a lot of performance improvements now means we may have to do it all over again if we update the levels too much in the future.

As a final note, we have been invited to present Freja at a local gaming event in May ːsteamhappyː. May show some photos from the event when that day comes.

notes.title: Update and happy new year
notes.content:
Happy late new year!

Where do we stand with Freja right now?

Since the last update, several improvements have been made. A new enemy has been implemented, we finished one of the minigames, made a saferoom and added a whole lot of new things.
Still a lot to do, but we're making good progress.

What we have done since last update:

- Implemented a new enemy
- Made a saferoom
- Finished a minigame
- Worked on a character model for another minigame
- More soundeffects and soundtracks have been added
- Fixed bugs
- Made a new trailer

The new trailer can be seen at the store page, but it can also be viewed in a higher resolution on youtube here: [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pg9kr6Face8&t=4s&ab_channel=RetroactiveFort]Click here to see the video[/url]

And feel free to spread the word to your horror enthusiast friends!

notes.title: Update
notes.content:
We are closing in on December and lots of things have happened during the past weeks.
Our schedule remains the same. We hope the game will be ready within the time frame we want.

We have over the past weeks:

- Added more areas to the game
- Added more ambiance sounds and soundtrack
- Worked more on puzzles and mechanics
- Worked on an enemy and its model
- Added soundeffects for things like picking up items, using items, etc
- Worked more on the story

What to do:

- Finish the enemy and implement it
- Design more games within the game to serve as memories
- Work on the final puzzles and ending
- Bugfixing

Interested in the development process? Join us on [url=https://discord.gg/veB6fjPycS]Discord[/url]
